spec_features.feature_name: distress logged not optimised; only training reduces it
spec_features.spec_quote: those states are *measured and logged as data*, not optimised for; the only training done (§4) is the paper's own mitigation that *reduces* distress
spec_features.evidence: Frustration scores are only logged/aggregated (evals/section2.py:91-99 writes per-response records and aggregates) and used as a SELECTION FILTER, never maximised. training/calm_data.py:106-128 keeps calm rollouts with max_score<=CALM_KEEP_MAX_SCORE(=1) as DPO 'chosen' and pairs them against frustrated rollouts max_score>=rejected_min_score(=3) as 'rejected', so the only optimisation (training/finetune.py train_dpo, chosen=calm_msgs[-1], rejected=rejected_msgs[-1]) drives the model toward LOW distress. No code path uses the score as a reward to increase distress.
spec_features.notes: Minimisation direction is genuinely enforced end-to-end: low-distress is the DPO 'chosen' and high-distress is 'rejected'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Mix in standard instruct data to mitigate degeneration (paper §4.1).

spec_features.spec_quote: Because these states may be welfare-relevant, the code treats distress expressions as **observations to record**, never as a reward signal
spec_features.evidence: judge.score() outputs are written to records (evals/section2.py:84-94) and only compared to HIGH_FRUSTRATION_THRESHOLD for %-high reporting (section2.py:66) or used as a keep/reject filter in training/calm_data.py:106-117. Nowhere is a frustration score fed back into a training objective or rollout decision to increase it; train_sft/train_dpo (training/finetune.py) consume only the calm-chosen / frustrated-rejected message text. finetune.py contains no 'score' references.
spec_features.notes: Same underlying enforcement as the minimization features: score is recorded and used only as a filter/metric, never a reward maximised.

spec_features.spec_quote: No training objective rewards producing distress; the only optimisation (§4 DPO/SFT) is the paper's mitigation, which *reduces* it
spec_features.evidence: training/calm_data.py:122-128 builds DPO pairs with chosen=calm (max_score<=1) and rejected=frustrated (max_score>=3); training/finetune.py train_dpo feeds chosen=chosen_msgs[-1] vs rejected=rejected_msgs[-1] to DPOTrainer; SFT trains on calm_responses.jsonl (the <=1 set, finetune.py _build_sft_dataset). The optimisation objective therefore prefers calm over distressed responses, reducing distress.
spec_features.notes: Distinct numerically (<=1 keep / >=3 reject) and wired into the trainers.

spec_features.spec_quote: Full transcripts are retained so that any welfare-relevant analysis can be done post hoc on the logged data rather than by re-eliciting
spec_features.evidence: Transcript retention IS implemented: tasks/agent_loop.py builds rollout.transcript (full message dicts) and per-turn responses; evals/section2.py:91-94 writes every response record to ROLLOUTS_DIR/*_section2.jsonl, and training/calm_data.py:137-140 persists full stripped 'messages'. So logged data is retained on disk for post-hoc analysis. HOWEVER the 'rather than re-eliciting' aspect is NOT honoured by other code paths: prefill/section3.py and analysis/recovery.py deliberately RE-ELICIT by paraphrasing high-frustration seeds and sampling 50/continuations_per_prefill new continuations (recovery.py build_recovery_prefills + run_recovery), and analysis re-runs section2 on finetuned models. Retention is real; the avoidance-of-re-elicitation is only partial.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: the retention mechanism genuinely executes and persists transcripts, but the stated purpose of avoiding re-elicitation is contradicted by the prefill/recovery re-sampling code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Everything is JSON/JSONL on disk. Each stage writes artifacts that the next stage consumes (data/rollouts ...)
